_note: New Madrid thread, extracted by reading every non-garbled passage the search returned. Model claude-opus-5, prompt v1.

mentions.claim_text: A massive earthquake on the New Madrid fault, the largest ever to happen on earth, splits the Mississippi River and makes it wider; every bridge on the river collapses and things are on fire.
mentions.quote: the largest earthquake that ever had happened on the earth
mentions.falsify_match: A New Madrid earthquake that destroys the Mississippi bridges.

mentions.claim_text: He expects the major New Madrid fault event to be the next big thing after the timeframe he has been describing.
mentions.quote: that major Madrid fault when I saw the python coming out of the water
mentions.time_phrase: about to see take place next
mentions.falsify_match: A New Madrid event follows the period he describes.
mentions.falsify_miss: The period passes with no New Madrid event.

mentions.claim_text: He ties the timing to the April eclipse crossing the New Madrid fault and to US pressure on Israel, citing a pattern of disasters following presidents who touch Israel.
mentions.quote: the Great American Eclipse goes over the New Madrid fault in April
mentions.condition_text: tied to US action on Israel
mentions.falsify_match: A New Madrid event in April 2024.

mentions.claim_text: He says the earthquakes he warned about are now happening on the New Madrid, citing seven in one day.
mentions.quote: I warned you about the earthquakes we see the earthquakes happening in the New Madrid
mentions.severity: seven small quakes in a day
mentions.falsify_match: Seismic activity records show a cluster of New Madrid quakes around Dec 2024.
mentions.falsify_miss: No such cluster in the record.

mentions.claim_text: He acknowledges people saying the earthquake has not happened, answers 'not yet', and restates that he saw a major New Madrid quake coming.
mentions.quote: Most people say, "We didn't have an earthquake." Not yet.
mentions.falsify_miss: Unfalsifiable as phrased: 'not yet' defers indefinitely.

mentions.claim_text: He states there was no big New Madrid earthquake in what he saw, only fours and fives, the fault line waking up and becoming active, while the California and British Columbia events he saw were large.
mentions.quote: there wasn't a big earthquake on that New Madrid. I saw shaking
mentions.falsify_match: Moderate New Madrid activity without a major rupture.
mentions.falsify_miss: Either nothing at all, or an immediate major rupture.

mentions.claim_text: If a two-state solution is agreed, three days later the New Madrid fault line splits in half and America is divided in half; Chinook helicopters carry supplies from the west to the central states.
mentions.quote: two-state solution, three days later, the New Madrid fault line will be split in half
mentions.condition_text: conditional on a two-state solution dividing Jerusalem
mentions.time_phrase: three days after a two-state solution
consequences: airlift of supplies west to centre
mentions.falsify_match: A two-state agreement followed within three days by a major New Madrid quake.
mentions.falsify_miss: A two-state agreement passes with no quake within three days.

mentions.claim_text: Thousands die in the event; houses built on cinder blocks are levelled while houses on foundations fare better; a tall building breaks apart and burns.
mentions.quote: there was thousands of people that passed away from this event
mentions.falsify_match: Mass casualties in a New Madrid event.

mentions.claim_text: Three days after a two-state solution splits Jerusalem, the New Madrid erupts with the largest earthquake in history and splits America in half; every bridge on the Mississippi is destroyed, cutting east from west.
mentions.quote: three days later after they split the... I saw the New Madrid fault line erupt
mentions.condition_text: three days after a two-state solution
mentions.falsify_match: A two-state agreement followed by a record New Madrid quake within three days.

mentions.claim_text: If the US agrees to divide Israel, people should run from the New Madrid fault line, because there are three days.
mentions.quote: then you better run from the New Madrid fault line. You better run
mentions.condition_text: if the US backs splitting Israel
mentions.falsify_miss: US backs a split with no quake in three days.

mentions.claim_text: The largest earthquake in history hits the New Madrid, destroying the whole Mississippi Valley and every bridge, stopping semi-trailers moving east to west, and shaking even the Liberty Bell.
mentions.quote: the largest earthquake in history hits that fault line
mentions.condition_text: framed as the consequence of a two-state solution
consequences: freight cannot cross east to west
mentions.falsify_match: A record New Madrid quake destroying Mississippi crossings.

mentions.claim_text: Tens of thousands of people perish, and the major houses along the New Madrid are completely destroyed. He appeals directly to the president not to back a two-state solution.
mentions.quote: there was literally tens of thousands of people that perished
mentions.falsify_match: Casualties in the tens of thousands.

mentions.claim_text: He gives a magnitude for the first time: an 8.4 New Madrid earthquake affecting Missouri, Kentucky and Tennessee, and tells viewers to write the number down. He frames it as a sign and a shaking to awaken, followed by revival in the heartland.
mentions.quote: I see 8.4. That's what I see. 8.4. Write that down.
consequences: people move back to the centre of the country
mentions.falsify_match: A New Madrid earthquake of roughly magnitude 8.4.
mentions.falsify_miss: No New Madrid quake above magnitude 6 in the horizon he implies.

mentions.claim_text: Asked whether the 8.4 is the Jerusalem-split earthquake, he says he does not know, and notes the earlier one he saw was over magnitude 10 while this one is a shaking to awaken.
mentions.quote: that one was over a 10, but I saw a shaking to awaken
mentions.condition_text: he separates the conditional Jerusalem quake from the 8.4 sign quake
mentions.falsify_match: Either event occurring identifies which branch was meant.

mentions.claim_text: He says he is worried about New Madrid because he saw many people die, and notes southern houses built on cinder blocks would not survive an 8.4.
mentions.quote: I'm concerned about New Madrid because I saw a lot of people die
mentions.falsify_match: Mass casualties concentrated in cinder-block housing.

mentions.claim_text: On the New Madrid he sees drought and a black rider on a black horse bringing drought wherever he goes, with famine of agriculture and money in trouble.
mentions.quote: I saw the black rider on the black horse riding upon the land
mentions.falsify_match: Drought and agricultural failure across the New Madrid region.
